result.title: Reinforcing intra-operative tumour localisation with weak supervision from pre-operative appearances
result.summary: Limited tumour visibility on intra-operative images complicates surgical navigation, including liver hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) targeting on computed tomography (CT) imaging. This makes labelled datasets difficult to curate for deep learning, and transferring pre-operative delineations through registration remains challenging due to intra-operative deformation and lack of paired pre- and intra-operative data. We propose to transfer tumour appearances learned from pre-operative magnetic resonance (MR) images to guide localisation on intra-operative CT through weak supervision. A classifier is trained to classify tumour presence on pre-operative images. This is applied to windows on intra-operative images, and despite the domain gap, it assigns higher tumour-presence probabilities on average to tumour-containing windows. These weak cross-domain signals guide a reinforcement learning agent to localise tumours on intra-operative images. We compare direct transfer, few-shot adaptation and synthetic transfer (trained using unpaired MR and CT), which translates CT into synthetic MR before localisation. On an external HCC cohort, synthetic transfer outperformed other tested methods and CT-only baselines. Our framework enables cross-modality tumour localisation without paired MR-CT training images.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在术前 MR 上训练肿瘤存在分类器，将其在术中 CT 窗口上的弱跨域概率信号作为奖励，驱动强化学习智能体定位肝细胞癌，并比较直接迁移、少样本适应与合成迁移三种方案。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把弱分类信号当作序列式视觉搜索的奖励，与 LVR 中主动选择视觉证据（LOOK）及弱监督下的证据贡献分配可能有概念联系，但任务与模态相距较远，仅供核查线索。
